Abstract: The strategic incorporation of auxiliary groups has recently established α-functionalized alcohols as
versatile electrophilic alkylation reagents, enabling remotely controlled conjugate additions. Strikingly, while
quinone methide chemistry has been extensively developed, their extended analogues—featuring spatially sepa-
rated carbonyl and methide units across biphenyl systems—remain unexplored. Building on the prior work with
alkynyl 4,4 0-biphenyl quinone methides, an organocatalytic remotely controlled enantioselective 1,10-additions
of in situ-generated alkynyl 2,40-biphenyl quinone methides from α-[4-(2- hydroxyphenyl)phenyl]propargyl
alcohols with 3-arylindoles and indole-2-carboxylates is reported, affording a broad scope of enantioenriched
3H-pyrrolo[1,2-a]indoles and axially chiral tetrasubstituted allenes, respectively. Combined with control experi-
ments, density functional theory calculations elucidate the reaction mechanism, revealing that the dehydration of
α-functionalized alcohols to generate 2,4 0-biphenyl quinone methides constitutes the rate-limiting step, while
enantioselectivity arises from the nucleophilic addition of alkynyl biphenyl quinone methides. Notably, beyond
proving 2,40-biphenyl quinone methides as competent intermediates, this work breaks new ground by demon-
strating their participation in previously unreported stereoselective 1,10-additions.

1. Introduction
The strategic design of auxiliary groups has revolution-
ized α-functionalized alcohol chemistry in recent years,
establishing these substrates as versatile platforms for
stereoselective electrophilic alkylation and related trans-
formations.<sup>[1]</sup> In this context, phenol and aniline have
emerged as particularly practical auxiliary groups,
enabling their corresponding α-functionalized alcohols
to in situ generate high-value quinone methides (QMs)
and aza-QMs, respectively.<sup>[2]</sup> These reactive intermedi-
ates serve as versatile platforms for diversity-oriented
synthesis.<sup>[3]</sup> In striking contrast to well-developed QM
chemistry, organocatalytic stereoselective reactions of
their extended analogues—where carbonyl and methide
units reside on separate aromatic rings—remain excep-
tionally rare. This stems from the inherent challenge of
exerting stereocontrol over spatially remote reactive cen-
ters in these systems.<sup>[4]</sup> To date, only three landmark
examples have been reported in this emerging field. In
2023, Sun and coworkers achieved a breakthrough with
the first CPA-catalyzed asymmetric 1,6-conjugate addi-
tion to in situ-generated 2-naphthoquinone-8-methides
(2-Nap-Q-8-Ms) and their aza-analogues (aza-2-Nap-
Q-8-Ms), derived from 8-(hydroxyarylmethyl)naphtha-
len-2-ols/amines for the synthesis of previously less
accessible remotely chiral naphthols and naphthylamines
(Scheme 1A).<sup>[5]</sup> Simultaneously, we developed the
complementary CPA-catalyzed 1,8-addition to (aza)-
2-naphthoquinone-6-methides ((aza)-2-Nap-Q-6-Ms)
from 6-(hydroxydiarylmethy l)naphthalen-2-ols/amines
(Scheme 1B),<sup>[6]</sup> enabling efficient synthesis of chiral
tetraarylmethanes.<sup>[7]</sup> Continually, we further pioneered
stereoselective 1,12-additions using alkynyl 4,4 0-
biphenyl quinone methides (4,4 0-BQMs) generated from
α-[4-(4-hydroxyphenyl)phenyl]propargyl alcohols for
construction of axially chiral tetrasubstituted allenes
(Scheme 1C).<sup>[8]</sup> Collectively, these advances systemati-
cally expand the auxiliary group design from basic
phenol/phenylamine to extend naphthol/naphthylamine
and biphenyl systems, creating a versatile platform for
CPA-catalyzed remote functionalization of α-substituted
alcohols. To further explore the chemistry of BQMs,<sup>[9]</sup>
and as our going interesting in developing α-functional-
ized alcohols,<sup>[6,8,10]</sup> we sought to expand the system from
alkynyl 4,4 0-BQMs to their 2,4 0-BQM counterparts,
focusing on the regiochemical flexibility of QM forma-
tion, the impact of altered π-conjugation patterns on
reactivity, and new opportunities for stereocontrol in
subsequent transformations. Herein, we report a catalytic
asymmetric 1,10-addition to in situ-generated alkynyl
2,40-BQMs derived from α-[4- (2-hydroxyphenyl)phenyl]
propargyl alcohols (Scheme 1D).<sup>[11]</sup> This remotely con-
trolled transformation demonstrates remarkable substrate-
directed divergence: 1) With 3-arylindoles, the reaction
constructs enantioenriched 3H-pyrrolo[1,2-a]indoles via
a dehydration/conjugate addition/annulation cascade;
2) Using indole-2-carboxylates, it forges axially chiral
tetrasubstituted allenes through a stereoselective dehydra-
tion/conjugate addition sequence. Notably, this work not
only establishes alkynyl 2,40-biphenyl quinone methides
(BQMs) as versatile intermediates for organocatalytic
asymmetric transformations but also demonstrates their
unique capacity to enable remote stereocontrolled 1,10-
conjugate additions and divergent synthesis of enantioen-
riched 3H-pyrrolo[1,2-a]indoles<sup>[10,12]</sup> and axially chiral
tetrasubstituted allenes.<sup>[13]</sup>

3. Conclusions
In conclusion, building on our previous success with
4-phenylphenol-based α-functionalized alcohols, we
have now demonstrated that 2-phenylphenol serves as
an effective auxiliary group for stereodivergent transfor-
mations of the corresponding α-functionalized alcohol.

General procedure for products (S)-3: To a solution of
CHCl (0.3 mL) was added propargylic alcohols 1 (0.06 mmol),
3-phenylindoles 2 (0.05 mmol), and CPA-2 (0.001 mmol). The
reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature for 48 h, and then
the solvent was removed under vacuum to give a residue, which
was purified by silica gel chromatography to yield products (S)-3.

4. Experimental Section
General procedure for products (S)-3: To a solution of
CHCl (0.3 mL) was added propargylic alcohols 1 (0.06 mmol),
3-phenylindoles 2 (0.05 mmol), and CPA-2 (0.001 mmol). The
reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature for 48 h, and then
the solvent was removed under vacuum to give a residue, which
was purified by silica gel chromatography to yield products (S)-3.
General procedure for products (S)-5: To a solution of CHCl
(0.3 mL) was added propargylic alcohols 1 (0.05 mmol), 2-indole
derivatives 4 (0.1 mmol), and CPA-7 (0.001 mmol). The reaction
mixture was stirred at room temperature for 24 h, and then the sol-
vent was removed under vacuum to give a residue, which was puri-
fied by silica gel chromatography to yield products (S)-5.
